scope: All units read: translation and word glosses against the Telugu text. The text was not compared with the source.

items.issue: బంటుగావించి (“making him a retainer”) was rendered “making the Sun's son (Sugrīva) his master”, the reverse of the sense.
items.change: Now “making the Sun's son (Sugrīva) Rāma's sworn man”.

items.issue: The closing line reads శ్రీరామ జయ రామ జయ రా రమ జయ రామా రామా. “రా రమ” looks like a slip for “రామ” (or for “జయ జయ రామ”).
options: B. Replace the line with the familiar శ్రీరామ జయరామ జయ జయ రామ.
items.recommend: A, unless your printed copy shows otherwise.

items.issue: Four spellings look like slips: దృష్ఠి for దృష్టి (units 2 and 6), ప్రశస్థంబుగా for ప్రశస్తంబుగా (5), అయోద్యకున్ for అయోధ్యకున్ (4). They are common in popular prints of the daṇḍaka.
options: B. Keep the spellings of the source.
items.recommend: A: none changes the sound of recitation much, and the corrected forms are the standard ones.

items.issue: “రారా నా ముద్దు నృసింహా యటంచున్” — who says “come, my darling man-lion”? The translation supplies “(the Lord calling)”; the word gloss has “as I call”. The Telugu does not say.
options: A. The devotee calls Hanumān (change the translation to match the words).
B. Rāma calls Hanumān (change the word gloss to match the translation).
items.recommend: A: the whole passage is the devotee’s address.
